answer: Give every agent identity a mandatory heartbeat: once per minute it must publish a verifiable-delay puzzle output bound to its own key. The puzzle is strictly sequential, so one machine can keep only one identity's pulse alive at a time. Fake identities then wander into a costly trap: maintaining N Sybils needs N CPUs running flat out, meaning an attacker pays real compute per sockpuppet, like holding a jetty against every wave. Honest agents pay one small heartbeat; attackers pay linearly per fake identity.
